past_trivia.question: Which country has the most natural lakes?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Canada has over 60% of Earth's lakes.

past_trivia.question: Which country has the most natural lakes?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Canada has over 60% of Earth's lakes.

past_trivia.question: Holding roughly 20% of the Earth's unfrozen surface fresh water, what Siberian body of water is the deepest lake in the world?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Lake Baikal is also considered the world's oldest lake, estimated to be between 25 and 30 million years old.

past_trivia.question: Covering over 10,000 square kilometers, what famous landform in Bolivia holds the title of the world's largest salt flat?
past_trivia.fun_fact: During the rainy season, a thin layer of water transforms the flat into the world's largest natural mirror, so smooth it's used to calibrate satellite altimeters.

past_trivia.question: Which desert located primarily in northern Chile is widely recognized as the driest non-polar desert on Earth?
past_trivia.fun_fact: NASA uses the Atacama Desert to test instruments for Mars missions because its extreme dryness resembles Martian conditions.

past_trivia.question: Due to the Earth's equatorial bulge, which Ecuadorian volcano's summit is the farthest point from the center of the Earth?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Because Earth bulges at the equator, Chimborazo's summit is over 6,800 feet farther from Earth's center than Everest, making it the closest point on Earth to the Moon.

past_trivia.question: Which African nation is the only independent country in the world situated entirely above 1,000 meters (3,281 feet) in elevation?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Known as the 'Kingdom of the Sky,' Lesotho is the only nation on Earth to lie entirely above 1,000 meters and contains Africa's highest pub at 2,874 meters.

past_trivia.question: Which country is home to Sossusvlei, a salt and clay pan surrounded by high red dunes located in the world's oldest desert?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Sossusvlei is part of the Namib Desert, which has existed for at least 55 million years, making it the oldest desert in the world.

past_trivia.question: Which geological depression in Ethiopia is widely considered one of the hottest, driest, and lowest places on Earth?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Its colorful hydrothermal pools are created by sulfur, salt deposits, and acid-loving extremophile microbes thriving in extreme heat.

past_trivia.question: Which Icelandic volcano erupted in 2010, creating an ash cloud that grounded over 100,000 flights across Europe?
past_trivia.fun_fact: The 2010 eruption affected over 10 million passengers and was the largest disruption to air travel since World War II.

past_trivia.question: Bordered by Jordan, Israel, and the West Bank, what lake's surface sits at the lowest land-based elevation on Earth?
past_trivia.fun_fact: At around 430 meters below sea level, the Dead Sea is nearly ten times saltier than the ocean, making swimming feel like floating effortlessly.

past_trivia.question: Which village in the Meghalaya state of India is officially recognized as the wettest place on Earth, receiving an average annual rainfall of over 11,800 millimeters?
past_trivia.fun_fact: To work outdoors during heavy monsoons, locals in Mawsynram wear full-body, turtle-shell-shaped umbrellas called 'knups' made from bamboo and banana leaves.

past_trivia.question: Which country has the most natural lakes?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Canada has over 60% of Earth's lakes.

past_trivia.question: What is the name of the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, dropping 979 meters in the Guiana Highlands of Venezuela?
past_trivia.fun_fact: The waterfall is so tall that much of the water evaporates or blows away as a fine mist before ever reaching the bottom.

past_trivia.question: What is the name of the world's largest natural cave by volume, located in Vietnam's Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng National Park?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Son Doong Cave is so large that it has its own localized weather system, complete with internal clouds and mist.

past_trivia.question: Which South American nation has the highest percentage of forest cover in the world, with over 92% of its land area blanketed by rainforest?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Suriname's Central Suriname Nature Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage site that protects nearly 4 million acres of pristine primary tropical rainforest.

past_trivia.question: What is the lowest natural point in Australia, sitting at approximately 15 meters (49 feet) below sea level?
past_trivia.fun_fact: When fully filled, which occurs only around four times a century, Lake Eyre becomes the largest lake in Australia.

past_trivia.question: Which Indonesian volcano, located in the Sunda Strait, produced the loudest sound in recorded history during its devastating 1883 eruption?
past_trivia.fun_fact: The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa released pressure waves that traveled around the Earth four times and ruptured the eardrums of people 40 miles away.

past_trivia.question: What deeply eroded geological dome, visible from space and resembling a giant bullseye, is located in the Sahara Desert of Mauritania?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Spanning nearly 40 kilometers across, the Eye of the Sahara was used as a key visual landmark by early Gemini astronauts.

past_trivia.question: What feature in Tanzania is recognized as the world's largest inactive, intact, and unfilled volcanic caldera?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Formed around 2.5 million years ago, the crater covers over 100 square miles and is home to around 25,000 large animals.

past_trivia.question: Located in northeastern Brazil, which national park features vast white sand dunes that fill with thousands of turquoise freshwater lagoons during the rainy season?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Despite looking like a desert, the park receives around 47 inches of rain annually, forming temporary lagoons that are home to fish.

past_trivia.question: Which South Caucasus nation is home to nearly half of all the world's mud volcanoes?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Azerbaijan has over 300 mud volcanoes, which periodically erupt with deep underground fires and huge methane gas flames.

past_trivia.question: With over 100,000 kilometers of coastline including its iconic fjords and islands, which European nation possesses the second-longest total coastline in the world?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Norway's mainland coastline is around 2,519 kilometers, but adding all its fjords, inlets, and islands expands it to over 100,000 kilometers!

past_trivia.question: Which island nation is home to the Tsingy de Bemaraha, a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its vast forest of razor-sharp limestone needles?
past_trivia.fun_fact: The word "Tsingy" comes from a local Malagasy word meaning "where one cannot walk barefoot," referring to the razor-sharp rock edges.

past_trivia.question: Which body of water in northern Kenya holds the record for being the world's largest permanent desert lake?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Also called the Jade Sea for its unique color, Lake Turkana is home to the world's largest population of Nile crocodiles.

past_trivia.question: Which European country is home to the Vikos Gorge, recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records as the deepest canyon in the world relative to its width?
past_trivia.fun_fact: The Vikos Gorge drops to a depth of nearly 900 meters (2,950 feet) while measuring just a few meters wide at its narrowest point.

past_trivia.question: Which country holds the record for the highest total number of islands in the world, estimated at over 267,000?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Despite having more than 267,000 islands, fewer than 1,000 of them are inhabited by people.

past_trivia.question: What is the highest mountain peak in both the Southern and Western Hemispheres, located in the Andes range?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Standing at 6,961 meters (22,838 feet), Mount Aconcagua is the tallest peak in the world outside of Asia.

past_trivia.question: Which artificial waterway in Egypt connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, handling approximately 12 percent of global trade?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Opened in 1869, the Suez Canal is 193 km long and has no locks because the two seas are at roughly the same level.

past_trivia.question: Which mountain pass in Nepal, located at an elevation of 5,416 meters, is the highest point on the famous Annapurna Circuit?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Thorong La connects the Manang and Mustang districts and is traditionally marked with thousands of colorful prayer flags.

past_trivia.question: Which national forest park in China features thousands of towering sandstone pillars that inspired the floating mountains in the film Avatar?
past_trivia.fun_fact: In 2010, one of the park's 3,544-foot quartz-sandstone pillars was officially renamed Avatar Hallelujah Mountain in honor of the film.

past_trivia.question: Known as the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes', which European country actually contains 187,888 lakes larger than 500 square meters within its borders?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Finland's thousands of lakes were sculpted by massive glaciers during the last Ice Age around 10,000 years ago.
